extracted.intended_audience: Principal Investigators (PIs), co-PIs, Sponsored Projects Offices (SPOs)/AORs, and NSF program/division officials
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and substantive reasons governing proposal withdrawals, returns without review, declinations, reconsideration requests, and resubmission after declination under the NSF PAPPG Chapter IV. Includes who may act, timelines, exclusions, and required formats for requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator’s Proposal Withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigator’s Proposal Withdrawal — allows a PI to initiate a proposal withdrawal and forward it to the organization’s AOR for submission to NSF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research.gov automates the proposal withdrawal process. A PI may initiate withdrawal via Research.gov which forwards the request to the Authorized Organizational Representative (AOR) for submission to NSF. Copies of reviews received by NSF before a proposal is withdrawn will be provided to the PI. If NSF has already made a funding decision, the electronic withdrawal will not be permitted and the PI should contact the cognizant NSF Program Officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsored Projects Office (SPO) Proposal Withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsored Projects Office (SPO) Proposal Withdrawal — allows an authorized individual in the organization’s SPO to initiate a proposal withdrawal and forward it to the AOR for submission to NSF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorized SPO staff can start a withdrawal in Research.gov and forward to the AOR. The withdrawal uses the Withdrawals Module in Research.gov and follows the same notification and review-copy procedures as PI-initiated withdrawals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Submission Duplicate Withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal Submission Duplicate Withdrawal — prevents the AOR from submitting a new proposal if a duplicate (a proposal from the same organization with the same title and same PI and co-PIs) already has been submitted to NSF within the last two weeks prior to the current submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the two-week duplicate condition is met, Research.gov will allow the AOR to either withdraw the previous duplicate proposal and then proceed with the new submission, or modify the new proposal so it is different from the previous proposal. This mechanism helps eliminate submission of duplicate proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized individuals' access to withdrawal functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized individuals can initiate or review a proposal withdrawal using the 'Proposal File Updates/Budget Revisions' function in Research.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AORs and other authorized officials (see footnote: AORs also can initiate a proposal withdrawal) may use this function to manage withdrawals. Use of the correct Research.gov function is required to effect electronic withdrawals.

rubrics_metrics.name: No withdrawal after NSF funding decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals will not be permitted to be withdrawn via the electronic proposal withdrawal system in cases where NSF already has made a funding decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an attempt is made to prepare a withdrawal for such a proposal, the system displays a message instructing the PI or authorized official to contact the cognizant NSF Program Officer for further assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to notify NSF if proposal receives other funding
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF must be notified if any funding for the proposed project is received from another source or sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If NSF learns that funding for a proposal has been accepted from another sponsor, NSF will send a withdrawal confirmation to the PI and the SPO without waiting for the official withdrawal notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative proposal withdrawal mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proposal withdrawal is submitted for a proposal that is part of a collaborative effort, the electronic proposal withdrawal system will withdraw that proposal along with the other remaining proposals identified as part of the collaborative effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies regardless of whether the organization is the lead or non-lead. If the remaining organizations in the collaborative determine that the project can still proceed, a new collaborative proposal must be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of review information upon withdrawal/return/declination
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of reviews received by NSF before a proposal is withdrawn will be provided to the PI. NSF provides notice of a withdrawal, return, declination, or reconsideration to both the PI and the SPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIs and co-PIs may access review information after the decision has received concurrence of the cognizant NSF Division Director, when all the review information has been released for their proposal (see Chapter III.G for additional info).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons a proposal will not be accepted or will be returned without review
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposal will not be accepted or will be returned without review by NSF for the following reasons: (a) is inappropriate for funding by the National Science Foundation; (b) has the potential to negatively impact research security due to credible information of a national security concern; (c) is submitted with insufficient lead-time before the activity is scheduled to begin; (d) is a full proposal submitted by a proposer that received a 'not invited' response to a preliminary proposal; (e) is a duplicate of, or substantially similar to, a proposal already under consideration by NSF from the same submitter; (f) does not meet NSF proposal preparation requirements (e.g., page limitations, formatting, electronic submission); (g) is not responsive to the NSF funding opportunity; (h) does not meet an announced proposal deadline date; (i) was previously reviewed and declined and has not been substantially revised; (j) duplicates another proposal that was already awarded; and/or (k) does not contain each of the required sections of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter I.B for 'inappropriate for funding' guidance. Proposal preparation requirements are specified in Part I of the PAPPG, the NSF Grants.gov Application Guide, or the program solicitation. Returns without review for national security concerns are expected to be rare. For duplicates, see Chapter I.G.1. Research.gov may prevent or block submission when 'Proposal Not Accepted' conditions are detected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declination notification and PI options
rubrics_metrics.description: A PI whose proposal has been declined will receive information and an explanation of the reason(s) for declination along with copies of the reviews considered in making the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the PI is not satisfied with the explanation, the PI may request additional information from the cognizant NSF Program Officer or Division Director. PIs and co-PIs may access review information after concurrence of the Division Director and release of review materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration — purpose and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposer whose proposal has been declined may ask for information beyond the explanatory materials and may request reconsideration to ensure NSF's review was fair and reasonable, substantively and procedurally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconsideration aims to ensure fairness and reasonableness and may examine scientific/technical merits within the context of budget availability and program priorities. It may address procedural errors in peer review, unaccounted-for conflicts of interest, or inappropriate consideration of records/information/rumor. Reconsideration is not adversarial; no formal hearing is provided; award of NSF assistance is discretionary so reconsideration may not result in an award even if error is found. No revisions made after declination will be considered in connection with the original proposal. NSF reserves the right to return without review a proposal substantially the same as one previously reviewed and declined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration applicability — exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF's reconsideration process is available concerning proposals for award funding but does not apply to: (a) 'discourage' (non-binding) decisions from preliminary proposals; (b) proposals for Fellowships, Travel, Planning, RAPID, EAGER, RAISE, SBIR Phase I, STTR Phase I; and (c) proposals returned without review for failure to be submitted with sufficient lead time, meet the announced deadline, or meet NSF proposal preparation requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers should check program-specific rules for additional restrictions. Excluded categories cannot use the standard reconsideration process described in this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial step in reconsideration — explanations by Program Officer/Division Director
rubrics_metrics.description: When a proposal is declined, the PI receives verbatim but unattributed copies of any ad hoc reviews and the panel summary (if applicable), a description of how the proposal was reviewed, and, if not otherwise provided, an explanation of the basis for the declination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A PI considering reconsideration should first contact the cognizant NSF Program Officer or Division Director, who will provide an informal opportunity for clarification prior to any formal reconsideration request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration by the Cognizant NSF Assistant Director (AD/Office Head)
rubrics_metrics.description: If dissatisfied after seeking clarification, the PI may request in writing that NSF reconsider its action; such a request will be considered only if the PI first sought clarification and the request is received within 90 days after the declination or return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request should be addressed to the AD/Office Head and explain why the PI believes the declination/return was unwarranted. The AD/Office Head will reconsider the record for fairness and reasonableness (substantively and procedurally), may request additional information from the PI, may obtain additional reviews (subject to standard review procedures and COI rules), and may designate another NSF official with no part in the initial review to conduct the reconsideration. The AD/Office Head will furnish results in writing within 45 days or explain the need for more time and indicate an expected date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further Reconsideration by the Deputy Director — organization-level request
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days after the AD/Office Head notifies the PI of the reconsideration results, the proposing organization may request further reconsideration by the Deputy Director of NSF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must be in writing, signed by the organization's president or other chief executive officer and by the PI, and should explain why the organization believes an error occurred in the initial evaluation or in the AD/Office Head reconsideration. The Deputy Director will review the record, may obtain additional reviews (subject to standard procedures), may designate another official who had no part in earlier actions, and will furnish results in writing within 30 days (or explain the need for more time). The Deputy Director's decision is final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission after declination — requirement for substantial revision and possible moratoriums
rubrics_metrics.description: A declined proposal may be resubmitted only after it has undergone substantial revision. NSF programs that accept proposals at any time may have guidelines establishing a moratorium during which a declined proposal (or reasonable facsimile) is ineligible for resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This moratorium allows time to digest merit review results and revise accordingly. A resubmitted proposal that has not clearly taken into account major comments or concerns from the prior NSF review may be returned without review. The Foundation will treat the revised proposal as a new proposal, subject to standard review procedures. Programs may specify the length of any moratorium.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF Risk Rubric (footnote)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation will develop an NSF Risk Rubric, comprised of risk-based indicators to inform the basis of return-without-review decision-making processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NSF Risk Rubric will be published on the NSF website. This rubric is intended to provide transparency about risk-based indicators used in decisions such as returns without review for national-security or other risk reasons.
